content.value:
HIGH-FLIP-RISK: TENANCY. Whether per-team scoping actually closes the disclosure, and whether the NO-SITES arm is reachable for a team that owns zero sites. Re-derive that judgment independently against the live control plane; do not accept this brief's framing.

CONTEXT. PR #11174 built a "Deploy health" block for the fleet digest and is OPEN and MERGEABLE. It is SUPERSEDED by this slice (charter D487, D493). Branch from origin/main and implement the whole thing here; the lead closes #11174. Read #11174's diff for the render shapes it got right (four distinct UNMEASURED sentences, the D3 rate shape, the try/rescue/catch so a DBConnection EXIT renders UNMEASURED instead of killing the send) and keep them.

WHY PER-TEAM, measured. #11174 threads ONE fleet-wide census into every team's email. All 13 control-plane sites belong to ONE team: fleet 24h attempts 841, team-506f 24h attempts 841, orphan site-less rows 0 — so the scoped census for the team that owns the fleet is BYTE-IDENTICAL, and fleet-wide buys it nothing. Meanwhile the 06:00Z send wrote 4 rows across 3 teams and TWO of those teams own ZERO sites, including frikk.jarl@gyldendal.no — the tenant this epic already has an open cross-tenant escalation about. And deliver_fleet_digest/1's own doc states the ruling verbatim ("Nobody learns of an instance they could not already read through the team-scoped instance list") while window_health/2's comment NAMES the cross-team hazard and then suppresses only the league table while shipping the totals. Half a rule is not a rule.

THE PLUMBING ALREADY EXISTS. DeployLedger.census/3 takes :site_ids (deploy_ledger.ex:810; scope_to_sites/2 at :1016-1020, where nil = unscoped and [] = no-sites are DELIBERATELY not collapsed). Registry.list_sites_for_team/1 (registry.ex:5141) accepts a bare team_id binary. router.ex:3855-3857 is a working precedent. Measured cost: fleet scan 26.9ms vs scoped scan 3.4ms; per-team is 6 cheap queries twice a day instead of 2.

WHAT TO BUILD.

1. SCOPE IT. Take the reading INSIDE the per-team comprehension in notifications.ex with site_ids: from that team's own sites. Expect most doors to fall below @min_sample 200 and render the counts-intact refusal — that is the honest answer, not a regression.
2. NO SITES != NO ROWS — this is a defect you will CREATE if you skip it. A zero-site team currently renders "UNMEASURED — no deploy rows at all in this window. A window with nothing in it is not a healthy fleet." For a team that owns no sites that is a FALSE ALARM dressed as honesty, delivered every morning. census/3 already refuses to collapse nil and []; the digest must render a DISTINCT no-sites arm for the same reason.
3. THE PROSE STOPS SAYING "fleet" on a team-scoped read — that is dr-w18-bl-census-headline-still-says-fleet about to be reproduced on a second surface.
4. THE ARITY PIN (D493). This adds a THIRD external DeployLedger.census caller, and deploy_ledger_reachability_test.exs:634 pins the external call-SITE multiset to [2, 3]. WIDEN IT TO [2, 3, 3] ON PURPOSE, with a comment naming digest_email.ex and why arity 3 (site_limit: 0 — the fleet RATE, never a per-site league table). Widen the PAIRED assertion inside the assert_raise at :643 too. Do NOT loosen to != [] or a count — the file's own comment says a new caller must edit the line on purpose. And do NOT hide the consumer behind a DeployLedger wrapper: Census.callers/4 buckets a site :internal iff the file IS deploy_ledger.ex (:91), so a wrapper holds the multiset at [2, 3] and hides the third consumer PERMANENTLY — the rubber stamp by evasion.
5. THE FANOUT FLAKE, one word, and it will otherwise red your Cloud gate at random. cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/push/fanout_result_test.exs:19 is async: true while asserting capture_log(...) == "", and ExUnit.CaptureLog is VM-GLOBAL — proved: it captures a warning from an unlinked bare spawn. A/B with a noisy async neighbour: 5/5 RED at async: true, 5/5 GREEN at async: false, both assertions untouched. The producer is Deploy.resume_orphaned/0's warning, added by #10476 two days AFTER cchi-w33-fanout-capture-log-async-true-asserts-the-whole-vm censused "zero async:true files log". Change async: true -> async: false and cite cchi-w33. Softening either assert log == "" to a substring match is REFUSED — it would let a future unexpected log line pass silently.

THE TEST SUITE CANNOT DECIDE THIS FOR YOU. All 27 digest tests render from hand-built fixture maps and never touch a database; 45/45 and 177/177 pass IDENTICALLY before and after scoping. Charter section 5232-5237 already ruled why: on the live control plane a production-drawn tenancy fixture is GREEN BY CONSTRUCTION. Your tenancy test MUST MANUFACTURE A SECOND TEAM that owns different sites and assert the two teams' rendered bodies carry DIFFERENT numbers.

DO NOT touch cloud/priv/static/app.js (fenced), deploy_ledger.ex itself (dr-w28-s4 owns it), or the digest's subject line.

GATE: cd cloud && CC=clang mix test test/barkpark_cloud/notifications/ test/barkpark_cloud/deploy_ledger_reachability_test.exs test/barkpark_cloud/push/fanout_result_test.exs
